source._version_note: Kafka 4.4.0 is released: its source and binary artifacts are in the Apache release area (downloads.apache.org/kafka/4.4.0/kafka-4.4.0-src.tgz, uploaded 2026-10-06, sha512 94E118D8...C6EACAC7, and kafka_2.13-4.4.0.tgz), which holds only voted releases. Upstream has not pushed a `4.4.0` git tag; the vote passed on 4.4.0-rc4, and the tree at tag 4.4.0-rc4 (commit 1156b275) is byte-identical to the released kafka-4.4.0-src.tgz (diff -r of the two trees, 2026-10-22: no differences; gradle.properties version=4.4.0). So this builds the released source from that tag. When upstream pushes `4.4.0` (same commit) or a later release, retarget_tag_pattern finds it.
source_prep: sed -i 's/^\(\s*\)reproducibleFileOrder = false/\1reproducibleFileOrder = true/; s/^\(\s*\)preserveFileTimestamps = true/\1preserveFileTimestamps = false/' build.gradle && grep -q 'reproducibleFileOrder = true' build.gradle && grep -q 'preserveFileTimestamps = false' build.gradle && ! grep -q 'preserveFileTimestamps = true' build.gradle
source._source_prep_note: The ONE source change: build.gradle's `tasks.withType(AbstractArchiveTask)` block sets reproducibleFileOrder = false and preserveFileTimestamps = true, so every jar and the release tarball record file modification times (the build's wall clock) and filesystem order: two builds of the same source never give the same jars. Gradle's documented reproducible-archive settings (true / false) give fixed entry times and a sorted order. It changes no code and no class file, only the archive metadata. Disclosed in the release note.
source._build_note: The online stage runs the full build once to fill /gradle-home (Gradle 9.6.1 distribution, plugins, every dependency) and then `clean`, so the offline stage compiles everything again from source with --offline: the image's jars come from the --network=none build, not from the online one. -PcommitId gives kafka-version.properties the release commit (determineCommitId reads .git otherwise, and the vendored tree has none). site-docs (the HTML documentation tarball) is not shipped in the image; the docs are at kafka.apache.org. upstream's launch script loads class-data-sharing archives (storage.jsa, kafka.jsa) that its image build creates by running Kafka; those two lines are removed, so the JVM starts without them (slightly slower start, same behaviour).

gradle_dependency_forces._why: Kafka 4.4.0 pins lz4-java 1.11.2 (gradle/dependencies.gradle); OSV: GHSA-mcr4-qmvw-px4g (high), GHSA-343h-94h5-c4wr and GHSA-gm45-99xc-r7wv, all fixed in 1.11.4, a patch release of the same line (metabase hit the same advisories on 1.11.1).

Kafka 4.4.0 pins snappy-java 1.1.10.7 (gradle/dependencies.gradle: snappy); Scout scan of the chain 727 image: CVE-2026-93451 (off-by-one) and CVE-2026-108106 (unbounded allocation), both high, both fixed in 1.1.10.9, a patch release of the same line (Apache-2.0, as 1.1.10.7). OSV lists nothing against 1.1.10.9. The jar sits in kafka's libs/ as snappy-java-<version>.jar.
